summary: Full backend + frontend testing of 409 Conflict handling for join requests. Backend: 19/21 tests pass (2 fail due to confirmed backend bug: rejected user cannot re-apply via POST /join). Frontend: 7/7 scenarios pass — notifications approve/409, owner vs non-owner Refuser button, participants modal 409 conflict-banner, cancel request flow.

critical.issue: When user has status='rejected', the join endpoint hits ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (doesn't update status back to pending) BUT falsely returns {success:true, status:'pending'}. The user's status remains 'rejected' in the DB. A rejected user can NEVER re-apply via the API — they're permanently blocked unless admin manually resets their DB record.
critical.root_cause: tagpoint_routes.py L746-754: after 'if existing:' block, if status is 'rejected' (not 'accepted' or 'pending'), code falls through to INSERT with ON CONFLICT (spot_you_id, user_id) DO NOTHING. The existing rejected row is NOT updated but API still returns the 'pending' success response.
critical.fix: Change INSERT to: ON CONFLICT (spot_you_id, user_id) DO UPDATE SET status='pending', requested_by=$4 WHERE spot_you_members.status IN ('rejected') OR add explicit handling: if existing['status'] not in ('accepted','pending'): update existing row to pending

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix POST /tag-points/{id}/join to handle status='rejected' case — currently ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING leaves DB unchanged while API falsely returns status='pending'. Fix: use DO UPDATE SET status='pending' for rejected users.

NOTE: Review request said admin@winek.app is the owner of pt_demo001 — this is INCORRECT. Actual owner is user@winek.app (user_demo001, Thomas Dupont). admin@winek.app is just an accepted member (system admin role). This affects: (a) Refuser button in notifications (only shown to spot-you owner, not system admin), (b) isAdmin in modal (only owner).
critical_code_review_comments: tagpoint_routes.py join endpoint L718-755: Missing handling for status='rejected'. Code: if existing: if accepted: return; if pending: return; [falls through for 'rejected'] → INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING → existing rejected row unchanged → false 'pending' response returned. Fix: add 'elif status not in (accepted, pending): UPDATE status to pending' OR change INSERT to ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET status='pending' WHERE excluded.status != 'accepted'.

Notification field naming confusion: The backend uses 'recipient_is_admin' to mean 'recipient is the spot-you owner/creator'. This naming is misleading — a system admin (admin@winek.app) who is just a member gets recipient_is_admin=False. The field name should be 'recipient_is_owner' or the frontend should check both system role and spot-you ownership.

rca_of_bug.reproduction: 1. Have user with status='rejected' on a members_approval SpotYou; 2. Call POST /tag-points/{id}/join; 3. API returns {success:true, status:'pending'} but DB status remains 'rejected'; 4. Verify with GET /tag-points/{id} — join_status still shows 'rejected'
rca_of_bug.root_cause: tagpoint_routes.py L718-726: 'if existing:' block only handles 'accepted' and 'pending' statuses with early returns. Status 'rejected' falls through to the INSERT statement (L750-755) which uses ON CONFLICT (spot_you_id, user_id) DO NOTHING — since a row already exists, nothing is inserted/updated. The code then returns the 'pending' response unconditionally.
rca_of_bug.mitigation: In tagpoint_routes.py, modify the existing check block to handle 'rejected': add explicit UPDATE to set status='pending' when existing status is 'rejected'. OR change the INSERT to: ON CONFLICT (spot_you_id, user_id) DO UPDATE SET status='pending', id=$1, requested_by=$4 WHERE spot_you_members.status = 'rejected'
